Cube world: the bake

Deep Time, cube plan phase 1, 22 October 2026. The bake can now write a planet as a cube world: format 0.7, the conformal cube turned freely, as you decided. It is opt-in (--set scale.projection=cube). Petroff-Guyou stays the default and is unchanged to the byte. The game does not play a cube world yet; that is phase 2.

  • WhatThe bake writes a planet as a cube world (format 0.7) when asked: --set scale.projection=cube. Petroff-Guyou stays the default and is unchanged to the byte.
  • ChecksB1, B3 to B6, B8 to B10 met. B7 met at 16k, the 4k planet's climate classes move more. B2 met from 1.5 simulation cells per world cell; between 1 and 1.5 the checkerboard leaks (a trade-off, not a bug; see B2).
  • Branchworktree-agent-a89a7cb292d951ee9, not merged. The synth commit is 0c922b3e.
  • NextPhase 2: the game reads cube worlds (the wrap engine joins the turning seams). Phase 4: the simulation on Moser's equal-area cube.

The planet on a cube

The planet is turned so that all eight corners of the cube fall in the sea, then unfolded into a net: four faces in a band (F3, F0, F1, F2), N above F0, S below it. Walking east off F2 brings you onto F3 (the slide). The other seams of N and S turn: their partner edges are not neighbours in the net, and phase 2's wrap engine joins them.

The colours are the world-map tool's satellite palette on the cube, the tile renderer's on Petroff-Guyou. The dark void around the six faces is not part of the world.

The 16k cube's provinces

Close views across seams

Each view is 320 blocks square, centred on a seam (the yellow ticks). A turning seam's partner side is drawn turned so the two sides meet as they do on the planet. No view shows a step, a colour edge or a broken river at a seam.

In the N east|F1 top view the edge between tan and green ground lies 60 to 80 blocks inside face N, not on the seam. The 4k views are an island and sea floor with impact craters; the shelves and rings run across the seams unbroken.

B2: the footprint, by band of its long axis

The bake reads the simulation through a footprint the size of a world cell, through the composed Jacobian. Where a world cell spans 1.5 simulation cells or more, a checkerboard at the simulation's resolution leaks under 0.03%. Between 1 and 1.5 cells it leaks 2.5% to 44%: a Gaussian wide enough to stop it there would blur away half of every four-cell feature. Under 1 cell the world is finer than the simulation and shows the checkerboard as it is (0.657 is the bilinear read's own response). Petroff-Guyou reads bilinearly, 0.657, wherever its polar widening does not reach.

WorldBodyRoleSemi-axes, blocksFrom the corner, blocksIn the net's voidRatio, exactRatio, SCL-091
4k cube152aureole62 by 1013816%1.381.39
4k cube183pluton57 by 883816%1.311.32

A body's horizontal ellipse is now the exact image of its planet ellipse under the composed Jacobian (SCL-130): its semi-axes are the singular values of J R(yaw) diag(a, c). The old rule (SCL-091, which Petroff-Guyou keeps) stretches each axis by its own image and overstates the area where the Lambert grid shears the two images off the perpendicular. A body whose ellipse holds a corner's image cannot be one ellipse. Round a corner the world has three quarters of a turn, so an ellipse over it covers a full turn of the net, and the quarter in the void folds back onto ground it already covers: about 4/3 of its planet area for any one ellipse. Those bodies are counted apart and listed; phase 2's per-face images are theirs. The first record read the scale at a body's centre alone, which misses that fold (it gave the two 4k bodies 1.007).

The relief across seams

The relief runs per face, in the local scale, and its noises are blended across turning seams so both faces read one value there (SCL-125). 16k cube against Petroff-Guyou: 51 and 51 active cones gullied with 8 gullies each, gully span 16.4 and 15.7 blocks, the jag on 529,535 and 505,100 L3 cells, cliff bands on 145,204 and 128,578, mean change 0.95 and 1.01 blocks. The block constants hold: gully spacing 8 or more, cliff bands 3 to 24 blocks, 4-block corners.

What the next phases need to know

Phase 2 (the game)

  • A river chain ending in a seam mouth (code 3) continues in its partner across a turning seam: carve them as one.
  • Structure windows crossing turning seams are kept whole (303 of 18,450 at 16k): the game must read them across the seam.
  • Bodies keep one ellipse, their centre's. Bodies over a corner (listed above) and the parts of bodies past a turning seam (52 bodies at 16k, 11 at 4k, up to half of one ellipse) need per-face images.
  • Spawn candidates keep 5 degrees from a corner and 64 blocks from a turning net edge; keep that margin.
  • Any noise in net coordinates breaks at a turning seam: blend it across as the bake's relief does (SCL-125).

Phase 4 (the simulation)

  • Near the Lambert simulation's poles its fans of stretched cells and stretched impact ellipses show through on the cube: the bake shows what the simulation made.
  • The footprint follows the Lambert grid's stretch; on Moser's equal-area cube it would follow the world's own cells, and the 1 to 1.5 band of B2 would mostly go.
  • The turn is applied after the simulation: compose it with the simulation's own cube when the simulation moves onto one.
